name: Music
description: What Windows is playing, with play/pause, previous and next — plus a live trace of how loud it is
author: Lattice

config.label: Show progress bar
config.help: Off keeps just the title and the buttons — some players report no duration at all.

config.label: Show sound level
config.help: The wavy line at the bottom. Off gives that space back to the controls and stops sampling.

config.label: Refresh interval
config.help: How often to ask Windows what is playing. App switches are caught on the next poll.

sections.title: It follows whatever Windows is playing
items: It reads the system media session, so Spotify, a browser tab and a local player all appear the same way.
Play / pause, previous and next act on that session — not on one particular app.
The card shows the track, the artist and album, and the app that is playing it.
A greyed-out previous or next means that player says it cannot skip — not that the widget is stuck.

sections.title: The wavy line is how loud it is
items: It taps what your speakers are playing right now, so it moves with any sound — a game or a video too, not just the track above.
It only keeps a number: no audio is recorded, stored or sent anywhere.
Nothing playing means a flat line on the baseline. That is the honest reading, not a fault.
No sound device, or one held by another app, also gives a flat line — the widget retries every two seconds.

sections.title: The buttons answer immediately
items: A click flips the icon at once; the next poll corrects it if the player disagreed.
Waiting two seconds for the icon to change reads as a broken button, so it does not wait.

sections.title: The progress bar
items: Turn Show progress bar off if your player reports no length — a bar that never moves is worse than none.
It is interpolated locally between polls, so it slides smoothly without asking Windows every second.
Seeking is not supported: the system media session does not expose it everywhere.

sections.title: Nothing playing
items: That is not an error. With no player open the card says Nothing playing and greys the buttons out.
Opening a player is picked up on the next poll, so give it a moment.

sections.title: Refresh interval
items: How often the card asks Windows what is playing. App switches are caught on the next poll, so a long interval lags.
The default is 2 seconds, which is below what the eye notices and still cheap.

changes: Renamed from Now Playing to Music, with the id lattice.music.
New: a sound-level trace along the bottom, like an ECG — it follows whatever your speakers are playing.
The card is taller and the layout no longer runs out of room at the bottom.
The player name is cleaned up: Spotify.exe now reads Spotify.
First release: read the system media session, with play / pause, previous and next.
Progress bar interpolated locally, so it moves without polling Windows every second.
Buttons flip immediately and are corrected by the next poll.
